clue.text: Quixotic giant in the theatre

definitions.meaning: Don Quixote tilted at mills with sails, taking them for giants
a famous London revue theatre in Soho

explanation.surface: A giant from Cervantes turns up on the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote mistook sail-driven mills for giants, and London's Windmill Theatre in Soho was known for its revues: two senses of one name.

clue.text: As dealer in exotic goods O Henry gives his real name

parts.note: an author introducing himself under his own name would say 'I am', shortened to I'M
the writer O. Henry was really William Sydney Porter

explanation.surface: A short-story writer, posing as a merchant of foreign wares, reveals who he truly is.
explanation.walkthrough: O. Henry was the pen name of William Sydney Porter, so his own introduction would be 'I'm Porter'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who brings goods in from abroad is a trader in foreign merchandise.

clue.text: Reads perhaps about study feature porcelain ware

indicators.note: about tells us the jumbled letters go around the other pieces
perhaps suggests the letters of the word may be arranged some other way

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: Someone reads up on porcelain featured in a study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reads perhaps' looks like a verb with a hedge, but 'perhaps' is the anagram signal; 'about' sends the scrambled letters round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain from Meissen near the Saxon city of that name is a classic collectable crockery.

clue.text: Like mortgagors to mortgagees indeed (accepting odd characters of both)

indicators.note: accepting means the word indeed takes other letters inside itself
the odd characters are the first and third letters of the word both

explanation.surface: Borrowers do owe their lenders, as the clue observes indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters of' picks the first and third letters of 'both'; 'accepting' tucks them inside 'indeed', which looks like an emphatic aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowers on a mortgage owe money to their lenders, so they are in debt to them.

clue.text: As Wells otherwise describes a criminal

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters of these words are put in another order

explanation.surface: The author H. G. Wells, put another way, characterises a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for someone who breaks the rules and disregards the law.

clue.text: The eye sees through what sounds comparatively trite

indicators.note: sounds tells us the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: more trite or hackneyed is cornier

explanation.surface: A remark about what the eye sees through sounds rather hackneyed.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNEA sounds like 'cornier', which means more trite.
explanation.definitionFit: The transparent front layer of the eyeball, through which light passes.

clue.text: Foreign capital, see, rising thus to the top.

indicators.note: to the top puts the upturned piece at the head of the column, above the other
in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: thus means so
lo is an old word meaning see or behold

explanation.surface: A foreign capital is seen rising to prominence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns SO into OS, and 'to the top' places it above LO.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Norway, a foreign seat of government from a British view.

clue.text: Walton's umber — a by no means colourful fish

parts.note: gray (grey) is a dull, uncoloured shade
the ling is a food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An old angling book names a dull-looking fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Izaak Walton's The Compleat Angler calls this fish the umber, an old name for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is an old name for the freshwater salmonid that Izaak Walton described in his angling book.

clue.text: Spray given first of all to Harpagon for instance

parts.note: the first letter of all, the start of the alphabet, is A
Harpagon is the skinflint in Moliere's L'Avare

explanation.surface: A spray is handed first to Moliere's stingy hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpagon is the hoarder in Moliere's comedy The Miser.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that turns a liquid such as perfume into a fine mist.

clue.text: Cheap selling during this recess

indicators.note: during means the letters are found inside the run of these words

explanation.surface: Cut-price trading goes on in this alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircular vaulted alcove at the end of a church is a recess.

clue.text: Let's hand out £25 for island livestock

indicators.note: out signals the letters of these words are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: Someone offers twenty-five pounds for animals from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LETSHAND into SHETLAND; a PONY is £25 in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hardy horse bred on the Scottish islands north of the mainland is an island animal.

clue.text: Colouring a point possibly about FBI types in it

indicators.note: possibly says the letters given could be arranged differently
about, in the sense of turned around, adds its weight to the jumbling of the pieces it sits among

parts.note: G-men are US federal agents, as of the FBI

explanation.surface: Colour on a point possibly concerns some FBI agents within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' and 'about' shuffle A POINT, G-MEN and IT together; G-men is American slang for federal agents, and 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural colouring of skin or tissue by deposits of colour.

clue.text: Certify return of Egyptian God in a race

indicators.note: in places the turned god inside the race letters

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: return of means the word is read backwards

parts.note: Set is the Egyptian god of chaos

explanation.surface: Someone vouches for an Egyptian god coming back in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns the god's name backwards and 'in' puts it inside TT, the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm formally or bear witness to the truth of something.

clue.text: A port to impress one who drinks too much

definitions.text: to impress one who drinks too much
definitions.meaning: to force a drunk man aboard as a sailor

explanation.surface: Somewhere on the coast, a heavy drinker is pressed into service.
explanation.definitionFit: It is China's great seaport, and also a verb for kidnapping a sailor by getting him drunk.

clue.text: Rich 'stuff for brother Jack, rebellious fellow

parts.note: Jack Cade led a revolt in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: Fine cloth is chosen for a brother named Jack, a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led a popular rebellion against Henry VI in 1450.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy fabric woven with raised patterns is luxurious material.

clue.text: Shakespeare contains note concerning this bride of Smetana

indicators.note: contains means the first piece holds the others

parts.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean note about Smetana's opera bride.
explanation.walkthrough: Smetana's opera is The Bartered Bride, so 'this' word describes the bride.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Czech opera the bride is traded for money, so the word describing her is exchanged.

clue.text: Is said to know ugly old woman, a provider of fodder

indicators.note: is said means the word is heard, not written

parts.note: one who is said to know knows
bag is slang for an unattractive old woman

explanation.surface: A hag reputed to be wise turns out to feed horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of feed hung from a horse's head supplies its food.

clue.text: Mounted attendant free to put in poor score on the range

indicators.note: to put in means one word goes inside another

parts.note: the outer ring of a target scores least on a shooting range
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A mounted escort is free to record a low score at the rifle range.
explanation.walkthrough: On a target the outer is the ring furthest from the bull, worth the fewest points.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider escorting a vehicle or procession on horse or motorcycle.

clue.text: Cupid has a maxim about the heart

indicators.note: the heart signals placing at the centre of the word

parts.note: a motto is a short saying or maxim
re means about

explanation.surface: Cupid has a saying about matters of the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the heart' puts RE in the middle of MOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A small love god or cherub in Italian art, like the Roman god of love.

clue.text: Thrown by one horse, do this or try another?

definitions.text: Thrown by one horse, do this or try another?

parts.words: Thrown by one horse, do this or try another?
parts.note: after a fall, a rider climbs back on, or takes a fresh horse

explanation.definitionFit: It means getting back into the saddle, and is also a fresh horse to ride.

clue.text: Soldier under obligation to be trustworthy

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
liable means legally bound or obliged

explanation.surface: A soldier who has duties ought to be dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependable and deserving trust.

clue.text: He quotes price of course that is below reserve

indicators.note: below means the second piece sits under the first in this down light

parts.note: to book is to reserve
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: He names a price for a course of action that's held back.
explanation.definitionFit: A turf accountant quotes odds on horses at the racecourse.

clue.text: Make: designs on a body for military display

definitions.meaning: an evening show of drill and music by troops

explanation.surface: Someone inks the skin of a soldier for a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both inking pictures into skin and an outdoor show of drill and band music by troops.

clue.text: His aim in confinement is to go 'places freely

indicators.note: freely says these letters are let loose to form something new

explanation.surface: A prisoner's ambition is to travel without restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who gets out of locks and chains wants to break free from bonds.

clue.text: Right type almost left, a character on the staff

parts.note: C for Conservative, a politician of the right

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A conservative type has nearly gone, a figure on the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol at the start of a musical stave fixing the pitch of the notes.

clue.text: Minimal amount is returned to you in France

indicators.note: is returned means the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: a toi is French for to you

explanation.surface: A tiny amount is sent back to you in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny quantity, from the smallest Greek letter.

clue.text: Choice (second one was natural for Darwin)

indicators.note: was says the word used to be longer before the letter was dropped

parts.note: Darwin's theory was natural selection
s is short for second

explanation.surface: A choice of the second type was natural for Darwin.
explanation.walkthrough: Darwin's 'natural selection' gives SELECTION; take away S (second) and what remains is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote or picking among candidates is a choice.

clue.text: Chinese princess's performance receiving a dowry at last

indicators.note: at last puts the next piece at the end
receiving means the word takes another letter inside it

parts.note: a turn is a stage act or performance
dot is a dowry, from French

explanation.surface: A Chinese princess's act receives a dowry at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Puccini's opera heroine is a Chinese princess; DOT is a word for dowry.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera is named after its Chinese royal heroine; the possessive is the name's.
